rationale: Amisulpride (full D2 antagonist) to aripiprazole (partial D2/D3 agonist). Common reasons: prolactin elevation causing sexual dysfunction or amenorrhoea, QTc concerns, desire for weight-neutral drug, or akathisia unexpectedly better tolerated. Aripiprazole's partial D2 agonism carries a significant akathisia risk when switching from a full D2 antagonist — patients stabilised on high D2 blockade may find the relative dopaminergic activation distressing. This risk is highest in the first 2–4 weeks. Cross-taper preferred over direct switch to allow gradual receptor adaptation. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start aripiprazole 10 mg. Continue amisulpride 400 mg. Counsel patient about akathisia risk — restlessness, inability to sit still, worst in first 2 weeks. Propranolol or low-dose diazepam can be used if severe.
Increase aripiprazole to 15 mg (target). Plateau amisulpride. Akathisia peak risk period — review at end of week 1. QTc risk begins to reduce as aripiprazole does not prolong QTc.
Reduce amisulpride to 200 mg. Aripiprazole at target dose. Insomnia and activation may emerge as amisulpride's sedative effect diminishes.
Reduce amisulpride to 100 mg. Monitor for sleep onset difficulties. Melatonin or short-term promethazine can bridge sleep difficulties.
Stop amisulpride. Continue aripiprazole 15 mg. Prolactin normalises rapidly after amisulpride stops. Counsel female patients about possible menstrual cycle restoration.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Amisulpride 400 mg ≈ aripiprazole 15 mg (Leucht et al. CMD method, Schizophrenia Bulletin 2015). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
